text: Reviewed all code files in the repository (Dockerfile and app.py). Verified L1 (missing USER in Dockerfile, leading to root execution inside the container) and L2/L3/L4 (SQL injection via unparameterized string formatting with request inputs in app.py). Leads L5 and L6 point to app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True), which is acceptable for a local/test lab or development environment as indicated by app.py/README.md, but noted or judged as expected development settings in this context. No other files needed review.

findings.title: Container running as root (Missing USER instruction)
findings.explanation: The Dockerfile does not specify a non-root USER instruction, so the container runs processes as root by default. If an attacker compromises the container, they have root privileges inside the container.
findings.fix: Add a non-root user (e.g. `RUN adduser -D appuser` and `USER appuser`) before the CMD instruction.
findings.description: The Dockerfile does not specify a non-root USER instruction, so the container runs processes as root by default. If an attacker compromises the container, they have root privileges inside the container.

findings.title: SQL Injection in lab login endpoint
findings.explanation: User-supplied username and password from request.form are directly interpolated into the SQL string without parameterization, allowing SQL injection.
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries: `c.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=? AND password=?", (username, password))` instead of formatting user input into the SQL string.
findings.description: User-supplied username and password from request.form are directly interpolated into the SQL string without parameterization, allowing SQL injection.
findings.code:
# Vulnerable SQL query construction (intentional)
        sql_query = (
            f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='{username}' AND password='{password}'"
        )
